newsitem.title: JAPAN: Traders say firm agrees to Yemen Q1 Masila price.
newsitem.headline: Traders say firm agrees to Yemen Q1 Masila price.

text.p: At least one company appears to have agreed to buy Masila crude oil for January-March 1997 from Yemen at dated Brent minus 97 cents, industry sources in Japan said on Wednesday.
Yemen said earlier this week that it had received bids from 20 Arab and international companies to buy crude oil for the first quarter in response to a sales tender issued last month.
A Yemeni official said the bids -- which had to be placed by November 25 and be valid until December 5 -- totalled 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Marib Light and Masila crude.
A price of dated Brent minus 97 cents was offered by Yemen in response to bids placed by the companies, Tokyo traders said.
One trader with a major said he believed that at least one company had agreed to the price.
Some traders said they would like to see a lower price, saying that without a further cut they doubted if they could make a profit.
But they said Yemen was unlikely to cut prices further.
Yemen exports about 100,000 bpd of Masila and 30,000 bpd of Marib Light to Japanese, South Korean and European buyers.
Yemen's price for Masila in the fourth quarter of this year was dated Brent minus 55 cents, while the price for Marib Light was dated Brent flat.
